In Port Harcourt, Rivers State branch of NUT, led by the state Chairman, Mr. Godfrey Nwogu, matched on a portion of Aba Road in Port Harcourt, calling for the unconditional release of the kidnapped Chibok girls.
Residents of Jos stormed the Jos Electricity Distribution Company, JEDC, over high electricity tariff, fake metres and other perceived 'gross injustices' meted on consumers in the state.

Scores of elders from Imufu Community in Enugu-Ezike, Igbo-Eze North Local Government Area of Enugu State, [16/06], protested at the office of the Permanent Secretary in Enugu, Rural Development in the state, protesting alleged plan to hijack the leadership of its Town Union.
Soldiers indiscriminately attack market shoppers without provocation or known reason. The soldiers may have been inebriated.

Militias from neighbouring towns fight over land in Share and Tsragi. No fewer than 50 houses have been reportedly burnt, 30 persons injured, while four persons were feared between the two towns, though more injuries may have come in Share.
No fewer than 1,000 residents of Sapele Local Government Area of Delta State protest poor electricity supply to the area by Benin Electricity Distribution Company.

assoc_actor_1: ASUU: Academic Staff Union of Universities
notes: ASUU members protest a labour dispute between government and staff of educational facilities.
A group of Igbo youths protest the outcome of the 28/03 election in Awka, Onitsha, Ekwolobia, Agulu and Nnewi. The protesters blamed the PDP for vote-rigging.
A group of Igbo youths protest the outcome of the 28/03 election in Awka, Onitsha, Ekwolobia, Agulu and Nnewi. The protesters blamed the PDP for vote-rigging.
Commercial motorcyclists at Ajibode area of Ibadan blocked the only motorable road to the area in protest of the death of two persons, including an okada rider. A similar protest took place in Apete.

notes: Protesters demonstrate against South African xenophobic attacks in Abujas SA embassy. Groups included were the National Youth Council of Nigeria (NYCN) and the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS). The protest forced a closure of the consulate.
Gunmen on motorcycles shoot and kill a police officer in the Tudun Wada area of the city for reasons unknown. Following the attack the assailants took the officers weapon.

The killing of about 200 animals(swine) by youths in Kafinkoro village, Paikoro Local Government Area of Niger State, reportedly led to a violent melee that resulted in the death of five villagers. The violence was preceded by a peaceful protest against the act.

Hundreds of youth in three communities-Onihale, Ilepa and Aiyede - in Ifo Local Government Area of Ogun State protested the alleged killing of a landlord, Ahmed Folorunsho, 26, by a night guard while pursuing robbers in the early hours of the previous day.

Three persons have reportedly lost their lives in the past two days (24/05 and 25/05) following a fight between youths of Shibiri and Etegbin communities in Ojo area of Lagos over collection of levies from tipper drivers transporting dredged sands from waterside.
Four unidentified gunmen have killed the newly sworn-in Ukanafun Local Government Council Secretary on a farm.
Youths riot after a traditional ruler not of their choosing is selected. One civilian bystander is killed the melee.
Militants (possibly kidnappers) attack residents of Igando. Casualties not known. Date not clear, on or before 07/09.
After a Ichen man was reportedly killed by unknown persons in his Megoge, Bagi LGA house, the victim's kinsmen blame Tiv, which led to a larger clash between the two groups.
Ugbene retaliate to the severe assault on one of their members by armed men from Ejuona by setting fire to Edjuona dwellings, leading to severe injuries.
Fulani headsmen attack Hingier Akaa at Tombo ward, Gaambe-tiev in Logo Local Government Area of the state killing one and injuring a second.
Between 10 and 15 persons were feared killed in an outbreak of fighting between suspected Fulani herdsmen and farmers at Ipiga village in Ohimini Local Government Area of Benue state.
Unidentified armed men attack the traditional ruler of Abba-Igogoro with a machete casing injury. Three others were shot and killed in the attack.
Suspected Fulani attack Gwantu killing a small child.
Youths kill a police inspector in a reprisal attack over the death of one of them who was reportedly shot dead by security operatives.

Hundreds of youth in three communities-Onihale, Ilepa and Aiyede - in Ifo Local Government Area of Ogun State protested the alleged killing of a landlord, Ahmed Folorunsho, 26, by a night guard while pursuing robbers in the early hours of the previous day.

Traffic on the newly constructed Shell Location Road, Orazi, in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State was disrupted following a protest by youths of Orazi community over claims that Shell Petroleum Development Company, had seized a portion of their farmland.
Activists burn a coffin in Lagos to express dissatisfaction with the call for Nigeria's separation and restructuring. Date not known, source dated 10/09.
A vigilante mob attacks and kills a cobbler after they suspect him of a recent stabbing.

Two sons of a traditional ruler, Chief Oliver Wobo, are found beheaded on 11/07 after disappearing on 10/07. Perpetrators not known. The ruler had passed away at an earlier date; the political power of the sons was not described by the source.
Two groups of youths violently protest for and against the postponement of an upcoming election. The unrest lasted two days. Several buildings destroyed. One death reported on the first day.

assoc_actor_1: NAPSS: National Association of Plateau State Students
notes: NAPSS protests over the transfer of a teacher.
Pensioners in Kwara State have protested in Ilorin over a Supreme Court decision that effects their payments.
A 'lunatic,' suspected member of a kidnap and ritualist gang was set ablaze by a mob, following the discovery of the gang's den in Mushin area of Lagos. Five were later arrested.

No fewer than 29 people were killed during a Fulani attack in Nkiedonwhro village of Irigwe chiefdom in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State on 16/10. A secondary source claims 48 were dead over several days, between 08/10-17/10.
Pensioners protest over pay in Owerri.

assoc_actor_1: NAPPS: National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools
notes: National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools, Ogun chapter staged a protest over alleged multiple taxation.
Pensioners protest over government funds at a state building in Abere.
Unidentified gunmen abduct a woman in Aba, Abia State. The date and the motive for the kidnapping are not known - source dated 22/05.

Residents of Atijere community in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State staged a protest against a recent invasion by gunmen from Imakun Omi in Akure. The attack is believed to be motivated by the areas oil deposits.
Market traders in Nkpor protest a tax on 27/04.

Hundreds of protesting workers demonstrated at a Shell Petroleum plant in Gbaran, Yenagoa Local Government Area of Bayelsa State over alleged violation of local content law and poor employment policies.
Two brothers and members of the Eggon tribe are beheaded by suspected Alago fighters as they travelled from Lafia to Obi in Eggon area.
Protest in Port Harcourt over forced eviction.

Hundreds of Ogoni youths in Rivers State blocked the Akpajo end of East West Road, protesting the location of the office United Nations Environment Programme. The protesters blocked the road for several hours.
Workers of a petroleum refinery shut their facility down and block its entrance over non-payment of their salaries.

Five persons were killed and four others injured by gunmen at Maraba Foron, Heipang District of Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau. Four of the dead were children with another victim being a member of the community's vigilance group, though it is not clear who the gunmen specifically targeted.
A group of market traders protest 'marginalization' by the state government in Sapele.
Anti-Tiv protest gather in Makurdi to protest recent Tiv related violence in Benue.

Shiite members protest in Bauchi, Potiskum and Birnin Gwari following the death of many of their fellow members in Zaria at the hands of the military, as well as for the release of a Shiite leader detained during the deadly raid.
Members of the Aga Orunto Ruling Family staged a peaceful protest to Ooni of Ifes palace over the appointment of new Obalufe.
There was pandemonium in Ajegunle area of Lagos State after commercial motorcycle operators known called Okada riders protested against the killing of a colleague by a commercial bus.
A group demonstrates against Senate President Bukola Saraki, calling for his resignation following the suspension of a fellow Senator. The protest took place at the national assembly.

Residents of five communities in Olorunda Local Council Development Area (Agemuwo, Agalato, Muwo Phase Two, Araromi-Ale, and Atiporomeh), Badagry Lagos State, on protested the demolition of numerous houses in their area, which left them displaced. The demonstration took place outside the Lagos State House of Assembly in Ikeja.
Protest at a fertilizer plant over plans of privatization.

Students protest at a Benin City government house after they learned an upcoming emanation coincided with an election date. The students, believing this would disenfranchise their vote, wanted the exam moved.
A young boy is burnt to death by a vigilante group after it was suspected he had stolen food.
Civil society groups protest the abduction of the Chibok school girls.

Workers at several oil flow stations in Delta State (Olomoro Flow Station, Olomoro Compressor Station, 1 and 2, Oweh Flow Station, Oroni Flow Station, Uzere Flow Station, Uzere Compressor Station, Afiesere Flow Station, Afiesere Compressor Station, Kokori Flow Station, Evwreni Flow Station and Ughelli Pumping Station) walk off the job and protest of unpaid salaries.
Midwives protest unpaid state salaries at the Lagos State house assembly on 05/10.
11 dead, including civilians, over a three day communal clash in Inyima village between its towns militia and their Onyadama neighbours over land. Exact causalities not known.
Youths and Hausa traders clash after a tax was demanded of them. It is not clear if the youths were representatives of the government. Two dead and a church was destroyed in the melee.

Clashes between Fulanis and farmers throughout Benue State, namely Agatu, Buruku, Tarka, Kwande, Logo, Makurdi and Guma LGAs, cause mass dislocation of the population. Date within the month and exact locations within the LGAs were not reported.
Suspected cattle rustlers attack Lilo, killing fifty. The attackers were also alleged to have burnt some houses and destroyed other property worth millions of naira.
Staff of Abia State Polytechnic block the entrances of the school in protest over salary issues.
07 January. Fulanis attack Awe community, three reported deaths.

Three persons are feared dead in Buguma, Asari Toru Local Government Area of Rivers State, after a clash between two groups identified as Kegema Unity Forum (typically populated with Kalabaris) and a second group known only as White Chelsea.
Oil workers protest the Nigeria Petroleum Development Company over pay on 31/05.

Students of a technical college protest, destroy property. The reason for the protest was not reported. Following the disturbances the school was closed indefinitely.
A group protesting the police seizure of commercial motorcycles clash with the officers. Injuries not known.
Militias from Ugbo and Ugbonla clash in Ugbonla over a chieftaincy tussle. One death reported.
Eleven are killed during a series of Fulani attacks around Godogodo.

Violence against residents of Ayama by militia from Isaba continued; several houses destroyed and seven villagers abducted.

About 500 supporters of All Progressives Congress, APC, in Idemili North and South federal constituency of Anambra State besieged the Federal High Court in Awka to protest alleged manipulation of the ticket for the constituency by the leadership of the party.
Two are killed by unidentified gunmen in Ukanafun LGA on 02/07.
Protesting youths destroy six buildings in Owheologbo community following domestic violence toward a kin.

At least 3 killed and five injured when unknown gunmen attacked people at the Kogi State polytechnic gate, Lokoja where senator Dino Melaye (APC) was holding a protest against the state government. Hotel workers protest Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, for defying a court order to vacate the hotel they had shut down and occupied since August 27.

Residents of Uhumnwonde Local Government Area protest at the Edo State House assembly over the suspension of their elected representative.

Scores of staff of Kwara State Water Corporation in Ilorin commenced a protest over non payments of their three months salaries which led to the untimely death of five of them. The staff locked the main gates to their expansive office along Sulu Gambari road Ilorin, and displayed various placards to express their grievances.

A visually impaired group protested over lack of availability of the white cane, which they use as a walking tool. They argued that the central government was not concerned about producing the cane within the country.

Fulanis attacked two Tiv Kwande LGA villages on 02/04 and 03/04, killing between 10 - 15. The attackers first targeted Ikyoawen, killing 4, before moving to Nzaav and Alaba in Yaav council ward, where over 11 persons were hacked to death and several houses burnt.
Suspected communal militia attacks a village in Riyom LGA, and are repelled by an armed group in the village. Causality details are not known.
Militias from Wanikade town and their Wanhihem neighbours clash over the use of farmland between 28/06 and 06/07. 100+ believed dead, property destroyed and 14,000 displaced.
Fulani gunmen opened fire on a funeral crowd in Yangal, killing seven and injuring 14.
Unidentified persons attack the motorcade of APC governor candidate Simon Lalong in Jos East, destroying four vehicles. No report of injury.
One killed and shops burnt as Muslim and Christian youth clash at Dan Anacha in Taraba following a confrontation over blasphemy.

Residents of Odioma community in Brass Local Government Area of Bayelsa State demonstrated at the office of the Chairman of the council to protest alleged plans to relocate a Fertilizer and Petrochemical Company to another area.

An attack at Rotsu village of Irigwe Chiefdom in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, has left one person dead and about 30 houses razed. The attack is believed to be related to a series of back-and-forth attacks between Fulanis and indigenes of the area.
A group of 400 farmers protest violent incidents between they and Fulanis. The protest occurred in several parts of Ido LGA, including Omi Adio, Onikanga, Mabolese, Alatori, Agbetu and Olorode.

Property destruction: Suspected arsonists set ablaze the Isiokolo office of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC damaging files and other sensitive items within the building. The fire is believed to be related to the recent election.

Students of Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Osun State protested over President Goodluck Jonathan's visit to their institution, demanding that he addresses them concerning educational funding (among other topics) before his departure. There was violence reported when two groups of students clashed, leaving five injured.

Aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Amuwo Odofin Local Government Area protested at the State Secretariat over the imposition of candidates. The protesters later went to a leader's office in Ikoyi and the state party secretariat to register similar complaints.
A women's group protest insecurity in the area, particularly in regard to herdsman attacks.

Four or five are killed by Fulani in Wannune during the overnight of 03/04. The following morning a group of youths protest the killings by barricading a road. Among the dead was an APC youth leader. The killings are believed to have been sparked after unidentified youths of the village killed two Fulanis early in the day of 03/04.

Following an attack on a Christian church, a group of Christian youths retaliate against a Muslim group - specifically not Boko Haram who are known to be responsible for the Church attack - and clash with them. Residents of Aghapalwa and Gwoshe communities were also involved in the clash. Over 100 reportedly dead with most of the village destroyed.

After a civilian is decapitated by Fulani attackers in Abraka, locals hold a protest over insecurity by taking the deceased remains to the palace of the Ovie of Oruarivie-Abraka and destroying property. Date of the attack and subsequent protest are not known - source dated 26/04.
About five persons reportedly lost their lives in a clash between two communities in Tai Local Government Area in the early hours of 07/05.
11 dead, including civilians, over a three day communal clash in Inyima village between its towns militia and their Onyadama neighbours over land. Exact causalities not known.

Clashes between Fulanis and farmers throughout Benue State, namely Agatu, Buruku, Tarka, Kwande, Logo, Makurdi and Guma LGAs, cause mass dislocation of the population. Date within the month and exact locations within the LGAs were not reported.
Unknown gunmen on 05/08 shot dead a yet-to-be identified middle-age woman in Osogbo. The incident occurred at about 9.00 am at Old Garage area of Osogbo. The reasons for the attack are not known.
Boko Haram (actor not confirmed) attack and kill a monarch and three others at Nkerefi in Nkanu East Local Government Area on 10/07.

assoc_actor_1: NANS: National Association of Nigerian Students
notes: Members of NANS locked the entrance of Lagos State University to demand the reopening of a building.
Eleven are killed when unidentified gunman attacked Zangang village in Attakar Chiefdom, Kaura Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The reason for the attack is not clear.

Members of a socio-cultural organization, Yoruba Liberation Movement, protested in Osogbo, Osun State against a statement credited to the former governor of Lagos State and National Leader of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Senator Bola Tinubu, that only three traditional rulers in Yoruba land are worthy of their stools.
Residents of Ado town protest, accusing the local government of unjustly taking their land.
Trader protest levies at Eke-Awka market.

Residents of oil bearing communities in Isoko nation, Delta State, have gathered at the premises of Heritage Energy Oil Services Limited in Ole(h), Isoko South Local Government Area, Delta State, protesting the company's alleged surreptitious takeover of asserts of the Nigeria Petroleum Development Company.
Members of IPOB protest at a Ekwulobia church during a service while the Anambra governor was in attendance.
Protesters mark the first anniversary of the Chibok abduction in Abuja.

Scores of students of the D.S Adegbenro ICT Polytechnic, Itori, in Ewekoro Local Government area of the state, went on rampage at the Itori end of the Lagos-Abeokuta Expressway, over the death of one of their colleagues who was reportedly crushed by a truck. The protesting students were said to have held up traffic for almost four hours, lasting from 11am till 3pm.
No fewer than 20 persons were on Friday wounded in a clash between rival youths at Ikpeshi community in Akoko Edo Local Government Area of Edo. The clash centred around the use of levied taxes.

Hundreds of protesters disrupted activities at the main entrance of the National Assembly, asking the Department of State Services, DSS, and anti-graft agencies to raid federal lawmakers in order to recover more public funds. Simultaenously, groups in Abuja converge to protest the state of the economy, specifically the fall of the naira.
Imo State lawmakers protest non-payment of salaries at the officer of the Accountant General.
Ten Micheal Otedola College of Primary Education students are injured during a unruly protest against alleged school corruption.

Members of the All Progressives Congress party stage a protest at the INEC (national election commission) headquarters in Abuja to register its disapproval of the Commissions string of failures in conducting recent elections, including the Delta Central Senatorial District bye-election and the inconclusive Anambra Governorship poll.
Commercial tricycle, Keke NAPEP, operators protest the killing of one their colleagues, who have disappeared earlier in the week.

Traders from Ibafon Main Market, Coconut area of Olodi Apapa, Lagos, protested at the corporate headquarters of Vanguard Media Ltd., protesting police extortion and harassment following several raids they considered unjust.

A group of APC women barricaded the entrance into State Secretariat of Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers, ahead of the visit of President Goodluck Jonathan to the place. Police dispersed the group with tear gas.

assoc_actor_1: ASUU: Academic Staff Union of Universities
notes: Members of the Academic Staff Union of Universities held street rallies in Onitsha and Awka, Anambra State, to press home their demand for the implementation of the 2009 agreement the union reached with the Federal Government.
Supporters of the Women Arise movement protest the killing of a civilian by police near a courthouse in Ebute-Metta on 25/11.
Beginning 04/01, Okada riders protest over a tariff until 07/01 in Ughelli, clashing with police on the final day, leading to arrests.
Staff of Federal Ministry of Information and Culture blocked the entrance of the ministry in protest of poor working conditions.

Students protest the continued closure of several campuses forcibly prevent the deputy governor from entering the Government Secretariat. The protest lasted for over an hour. This was the second consecutive day of protesting.

Security forces guarding a petroleum pipeline clash with police forces, one dead. The clash began after the security forces began impounding illegally parked vehicles around the facility, which led to a confrontation with police.
Members of the National Youth Council of Nigeria stage a protest over the deaths of their colleagues during an auto accident.
Protest after Patience Jonathans (former First Lady) assets are frozen over money laundering claims.

Suspected (Fulani) herdsmen attacked a farm settlement at Umueze near Oloa-Ossissa community, Ndokwa East Local Government Area, Delta State, killing a 15-year-old boy and inflicting bullet wounds on his father.
Property destruction: A local party office of the APC is destroyed with dynamite during the early hours of the day. It is not believed that anyone was inside or harmed.

Clashes between Fulanis and farmers throughout Benue State, namely Agatu, Buruku, Tarka, Kwande, Logo, Makurdi and Guma LGAs, cause mass dislocation of the population. Date within the month and exact locations within the LGAs were not reported.
Suspected Fulani herdsmen raided a prison at Jato Aka, killing an inmate. The attack led to a riot among the other inmates.
Militias from Oku Iboku and Ikot Offiong clash over two days over suspected boundary issues. Twenty dead.
Labours protest non-payment of contracts in Port Harcourt on 29/12.
Militias from Wanikade town and their Wanhihem neighbours clash over the use of farmland between 28/06 and 06/07. 100+ believed dead, property destroyed and 14,000 displaced.
Members of the local Bar Association led lawyers in the state to protest bail conditions announced by the state judiciary.
Numbering 2,000, Sapele residents protest prolonged power outages in their area.

assoc_actor_1: FRPSO: Forum of 2011/12 Retired Public Servants of Osun
notes: Pensioners under the aegis of 'Forum of 2011/12 Retired Public Servants of Osun' on 30/06 barricaded the entrance to the Government Secretariat, preventing workers from entering their offices. The protest was over the non-payment of stipends. The protest began the previous day, with protesters blocking Olaiya Junction.
Six persons were killed and two others injured when suspected Fulani gunmen attacked Gambiri village in Ganjuwa Local Government Area of Bauchi State.

Business activities were grounded at the headquarters of the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, as a result of a protest staged against the commission's management by workers. There was a similar protest in Lagos.
Polytechnic students barricaded the entrance of their school in protest of a registration fee. A similar protest occurred the previous day.

No fewer than 10 persons sustained various degrees of injury, while about five others were arrested by the police in a clash over the ownership of a large expanse of land where the abandoned airport project at Oba, Idemili South Local Government Area of Anambra State is situated.
Armed students attack their teachers with blunt weapons and cause damage to their on 16/02. The reasons for the violence is not known. Injuries, causalities not known.
A group of Okada motorcyclists assaulted a police officer and stole his motorcycle on the road connecting Oshodi and Apapa. The reason for the attack is not known.
Five persons have been allegedly killed by youths in Eyobisung village in Udung Uko local government areas of Akwa Ibom State. The youths accused the victims of witchcraft.
Two unidentified armed robbers were burnt to death by residents of Nyong Edem Street off White House, Calabar.
11 dead, including civilians, over a three day communal clash in Inyima village between its towns militia and their Onyadama neighbours over land. Exact causalities not known.

Staff of the Nigerian Petroleum Development Company, NPDC attached to the Eriemu oil field, Ughelli North Local Government Area, Delta State, embarked on a protest against the alleged non-payment of their six months' salaries and bonuses.

A pastor or cleric is targeted for abduction by unidentified gunmen in Uromi on 25/12. Though the kidnapping was ultimately unsuccessful, the attackers shot and severely injured a guard. The motive for the attack is not yet known.
For the second day, members of the Aga Orunto Ruling Family staged a peaceful protest to Ooni of Ifes palace over the appointment of new Obalufe.

Former vice chairman of Patani local government area was abducted by gunmen and whisked away to an unknown location. The victim was abducted along Isoko Road, close to Uloho Avenue junction. The reason for the abduction is not known.
Two Cross River communities clash over three days in Yakurr LGA. Causalities not known. On the final day militia from Mkpani clashed with soldiers they mistook for mercenaries.
Protesters block the entrance to the National Assembly, calling for the prosecution of the alleged corruption of judges. The protest lasted for two days.

Residents of Arepo, a community along Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Ogun State, protest against a government plan to block an access road to pave the way for a health centre. which would require the destruction of local shops.
Fulanis attack Etogi community in Gbara ward in Mokwa local government killing 27.

actor1: NDGJM: Niger Delta Greenland Justice Mandate
notes: NDGJM, on the morning of 27/11, blew up a pipeline operated by the Nigerian Petroleum Development Company, NPDC in Otu-Jeremi, Ughelli South, Delta State.
A vigilante group attacks and sets two suspected thieves alight on Gboko on 02/04.
Two Cross River communities clash over three days in Yakurr LGA. Causalities not known. On the final day militia from Mkpani clashed with soldiers they mistook for mercenaries.

Following the suspected police shooting of Senator Abe in Rumuola people protest in his home district. The supporters believe the shooting of senator Abe was an attempt to stop the Ogoni people from producing a governor for the state in 2015.

The police in Gwagwalada (FCT), Abuja, have confirmed that four people were killed and 19 others injured in a clash between Gwari farmers and Fulani herdsmen in Paiko, near Gwagwalada. It was learned the Fulani attacked the town, which caused a reaction from the local Gbagyi, sparking the clash.
Violent protest at a Lokoja hotel after a guest died in its swimming pool.
Unidentified persons have reportedly executed the village head and youth leader of Ikot Anta Enen Obom village, Ukanafun Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State on 24/01.
Residents of Awada Obosi in Idemili North Local Government Area of Anambra State 22/06 took to streets to protest what they described as poor electricity supply and high bills.
Traders at Alaba International Market, near Lagos State University, protest over land encroachment by a bank.
Three suspected robbers were lynched by youths when they robbed the residence of one Abdulmumini Daga and three others in Daga village, Jibia Local Government Area of Katsina State.
A suspected thief is beaten to death by a vigilante mob in Amorji Nike, Abakpa in Enugu East.

At least 11 persons have been feared killed at Ganlang village at Zamadede of Pil-Gani district of Langtang North Local Government Area of Plateau State after unidentified gunmen, suspected to be Fulani, attacked the village during the early morning hours.
Hundreds of doctors took to major streets in Lagos, Ibadan, Akure in Ondo State, to protest against the purported sacking of 16,000 resident doctors.
A vigilante mob beats a suspected thief death at Twon Brass.
Members and supporters of WAI, among others, protest a pastor was had been accused of sexually abusing children.
Members of the Anambra State Vigilante group protested the non-payment of their eight months salary arrears by the state government. The protest took place at the government house in Awka.

University of Benin students protest the recent demolition of parts of university by the Edo state government for a second day. The group attacked property of the Edo State Government, set a bus alight, and blocked the entire Benin-Lagos Road for over two hours before armed soldiers and Policemen were deployed to disperse them.
Unidentified gunmen abduct 40 in Maru LGA.

Constitutional lawyers and human rights activists from various parts of the country staged a protest in Abuja against the continued detention of former National Security Adviser. The protesters complained the person remained detained despite several payments of bail.

Four persons from Aguleri, Anambra East local government area were killed on Monday, while seven others were seriously injured in a renewed clash between the people of Aguleri and Echeno/Odeke in Ibaji local government area of Kogi State. The two groups were fighting over rights to oil production in the area. It is not clear if the Echeno/Odeke fighters were organized around ethnicity, or simply residents of the area.
Federal retirees under the aegis of Nigeria Union of Pensioners protested non payment of their 10 months contributory pension in Abeokuta.
A cameraman with the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS), Mr Ikechukwu Onubogu, has been found dead four days after he was declared missing. The date of death and perpetrators not known.

Residents of Abavo community attempt to invade the local monarchs palace in an effort to unseat the ruler. Five houses destroyed and many wounded during a clash with the palace guards. The unrest is likely linked to the rights to oil recently discovered in the area.
Ijaw youths shot and cut off the head of an Urhobo youth residing at Aladja, Udu Local Government Area in revenge of a beheading of a Ogbe-Ijoh carpenter on 09/12.
05 July. Lorry drivers block the Enugu -Onitsha highway outside of Onitsha by stopping their trucks in protest of the poor state of the road.
Suspected Fulanis attack Zakupwang community, Foron District and Fan village in Fan District of Barkin Ladi Local Government council on 13/09. Twenty dead between the two towns.

Policemen barricaded the two ends of Moscow Road leading to the state House of Assembly, thus preventing the pro-Governor Chibuike Amaechi lawmakers from reconvening the House. Police forces also implemented tear gas on the crowd. The previous day a court order declared it illegal for lawmakers to take over of the legislative functions of the Rivers State House of Assembly by the House of Representatives.

assoc_actor_1: ASUP: Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics
notes: Members of ASUP protest insecurity following the murder (details unknown) of a priest.

Residents from Ita Sanni, Gbaga, Ogijo, Odogunyan, Agbede, 1st Gate, Okegbegun and Ikorodu in Lagos and Ogun states protested poor condition of Ikorodu/Sagamu road which they claimed has recorded many untimely deaths.
Party violence among the APC at a political rally in Dobi causes one death. Eight arrested the following day.

Residents from Ita Sanni, Gbaga, Ogijo, Odogunyan, Agbede, 1st Gate, Okegbegun and Ikorodu in Lagos and Ogun states protested poor condition of Ikorodu/Sagamu road which they claimed has recorded many untimely deaths.
Abductors kidnapped an army Colonel while he travelled with his wife in Kamaza on 26/03. The colonel was later found dead.
1,000 youths of Nkwelle-Ezunaka community in Oyi Local Government Area of Anambra state, took to the major roads in protest against what they termed alleged plot to remove their town union executive.

assoc_actor_1: KYAN: Kibaku Youth Association of Nigeria
notes: Youths, under the aegis of Kibaku Youth Association of Nigeria, KYAN, stormed the office of Governor Babatunde Fashola of Lagos State to protest the continued abduction of 234 female students of Government Girls Secondary School, Chibok Local Government, Borno State by the Boko Haram insurgents and called for their immediate release.

The Speaker of the Edo State House of Assembly and 14 other All Progressives Congress (APC) lawmakers escaped death after over one hundred armed mobile policemen deployed from Abuja to the state, took over the premises of the state House of Assembly. The policemen who stormed the Assembly complex at about 11am started assaulting the staff of the Assembly in their offices, ordering them out of the premises. The police came to carry out a court order which barred four members of the assembly from entering the government house.
27 April. Eight persons are feared dead after suspected herdsmen (Fulani) invaded Agagbe community, Gwer West Local Government Area of Benue State.
Staff and students of Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU) Ile-Ife, staged violent protest at the premises of the State High Court, Ede after the former Acting Vice Chancellor was sentenced to prison.

assoc_actor_1: NULGE: Nigerian Union of Local Government Employees
notes: NUGLE workers protest inaction by the state government to pass a law to their benefit. The protest was staged outside the state house building in Akure.
Residents of Igbatoro, Akure North LGA protest a Fulani attack which killed a farmer in the area in recent weeks.
A group of heavily armed men attack Ilase (Ilashe) the morning of 10/04, but were repelled by police forces. One civilian is believed to have been shot, fate unknown.
A suspected suicide bomber of unknown origin rammed an automobile into a military checkpoint in Bajoga. No heavy damage reported.
An angry mob at Sawmill area of Ilorin burnt a middle aged woman to death for allegedly kidnapping five children.
Yoruba and Hause militias clash in Kosofe the night of 02/03. Four reported dead from fighting.

assoc_actor_1: OSTTO: Ondo State Timbers Traders Organization
notes: Members of the Ondo State Timbers Traders Organization, OSTTO, blocked the entrance to the governor's office while protesting the continued closure of forest reserves and banning of logging activities by the state government.

Four or five are killed by Fulani during the overnight of 03/04. The following morning a group of youths protest the killings by barricading a road in Wannune. Among the dead was an APC youth leader. The killings are believed to have been sparked after unidentified youths of the village killed two Fulanis early in the day of 03/04.

Soldiers went on rampage, grounding human and vehicular movements along Ikorodu road, Lagos, following allegations that a commercial bus belonging to the Lagos State government ran over one of them, killing him at the Palmgrove bus stop at about 9:00 am. The soldiers alleged that a Rapid Transport Bus, BRT, vehicle killed one of their colleagues at Palmgrove. They reportedly burnt any BRT vehicle on sight during the rampage. The soldiers barricaded both sides of the road in the process. Some persons were also injured following the ensuing rampage.
Five are dead after members of Igbide community attack Okpolo-Enhwe community on 07/05 in a boundary dispute.
Residents around the nation protest high electricity bills in Ikeja. The protest was organized by the NCP.
Numbering in the hundreds, youths protest the planned prosecution of a Synagogue after its building collapsed in 2014.

Scores of residents of Ijora-Badia protested at the local Police Station after the alleged killing of two youths by policemen in the area. According to eyewitnesses, the two were killed earlier in the day (Sunday) while policemen were attempting to disperse youths who were engaged in a street brawl.

Clashes between Fulanis and farmers throughout Benue State, namely Agatu, Buruku, Tarka, Kwande, Logo, Makurdi and Guma LGAs, cause mass dislocation of the population. Date within the month and exact locations within the LGAs were not reported.

Four are dead in a communal clash between two groups fighting over a fish pond in Iyamu, a remote community in Ibaji Local Government Area of Kogi State. The identities of the perpetrators are not known.

Unionized members of a electricity company union, the Power Holdings Company of Nigeria, hold a nation-wide protest President Jonathans decision to convert the controlling stake of the organization to private management.
A Christian group protests after it was suspered a member was killed by a Muslim group or individual.

The women's wing of Isoko Development Union, IDU, protests against warring Igbide and Okpolo-Enwhe communities in Isoko South Local Government Area, Delta State, demanding an end to hostilities. The protest took place in Igbide.
Residents of Ijegun Egba Waterside community protested the poor condition of Buba Marwa Road in Oriade Local Council Development Area. Police were present, but did not engage the protesters.
Armed youths of Odiemerenyi community, Ahoada East attack a group of oil inspectors after an extortion payment is denied.
A protest against poor roads is led by a 90-year-old woman in Okoroba.
Some commercial farmers at Oke Ako -Ipao axis of Ekiti State protested the alleged destruction of crops by Fulanis.

assoc_actor_1: PENGASSAN: Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria
notes: PENGASSAN workers continue a protest for a second day.
A 70-year-old woman led a group of protesters over the last months murder of her son. The group called for re-opening of a police investigation.

Some members of Enugu State chapter of All Progressives Congress, APC, fought at the state office secretariat. Although the cause of the fight is not known, state chairman of the party blamed the incident on alleged attempt by some members, alleged to be moles, to cause disaffection in the party. Injuries not known.
Pensioners block roads in Benin City over a non-payment issue with their stipends.
Members of IPOB protest at a Rivers State police station for the release of one of their members. The location was not named by the source. The release was granted.

Fulanis attacked two Tiv Kwande LGA villages on 02/04 and 03/04, killing between 10 - 15. The attackers first targeted Ikyoawen before moving to Nzaav and Alaba in Yaav council ward, where more people were killed.
An explosion in a Oworonsoki beer parlour injures five in 11/10. Perpetrators not known.
Students protest alleged government corruption, particularly that of the governor.

A number labour unions protest unfair labour practices in a march through Lagos. National Union of Textile Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN), National Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers, NUPENG, Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, PENGASSAN, Chemical and Non-Metallic Products Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, CANMPSSAN, and National Union of Chemical, Footwear, Rubber, Leather and Non Metallic Products Employees, NUCFRLANMPE. Civil society allies under the Joint Action Forum, JAF, Democratic Socialist Movement, DSM, and Campaign for Workers Democratic Rights.

A youth in Ayama, an outpost of Aladja, Udu Local Government Area, was reportedly shot dead by men from neighbouring Isaba, Warri South West, Delta State in communal conflict. A second victim was reported missing.
Members of some Non-Governmental Organisations, NGOs and petty traders stormed the Lagos State House of Assembly, protesting against the state governments ban on street trading in the state.
Militias from Wanikade town and their Wanhihem neighbours clash over the use of farmland between 28/06 and 06/07. 100+ believed dead, property destroyed and 14,000 displaced.
200 workers of a detergent firm protest their termination. The protest lasted three consecutive days.
One person died while two were abducted in a clash between Ijaw community of Ezebiri and their Urhobo counterpart at Furukama in Bomadi and Ughelli South Local Government Areas of Delta State.

Some supporters of President Muhammadu Buhari clashed with members of the #BringBackOurGirls group, as the campaigners made their way to the Presidential Villa in Abuja. The supporters of the president believed the campaigners meant to undermine the APC.
Hundreds of Ugbo Okonkwo residents staged a peaceful protest against plans by Enugu State Government to demolish their houses in the area which it designated as a slum.

Students of Yaba College of Technology, YABATECH, protested the death of a fellow student, alleging medical malpractice and a transfer policy. Students were also protesting at the nearby University of Lagos, also on Lagos Mainland. The protest was violent and is expected to cause the university to close for several weeks.
Touts and transporters clash over rights to a motor park on 11/05. Police move in, avert bloodshed. Two arrests reported.
2 killed, 2 injured, 3 missing in hostilities between militias of Igbide and Okpolo-Enwhe towns in Isoko South LGA, Delta. The dispute arose over land.
A group of Igbo youths protest the outcome of the 28/03 election in Awka, Onitsha, Ekwolobia, Agulu and Nnewi. The protesters blamed the PDP for vote-rigging.
Lepers stage a road blocking protest, demanding more government stipends. Fearing the disease, many area residents fled the area.

Nine persons including a personnel of Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSDC were reportedly killed while ten others sustained various degrees of injuries when Fulanis attacked Ibi and Wukari local government areas of Taraba State on 25/02.
Factionist members of NUP protest the result of a leadership election outside their secretariat in Enugu.
Suspected Fulanis attack several unnamed villages in Gwer West, killing 35 and over two days. The exact dates are not clear.
Unidentified gunmen kidnap the brother of the monarch of the of Kolokuma Kingdom, their demands not known.
A suspected rapist nearly is victim of a vigilante lynch mob before being rescued by police.

assoc_actor_1: FONGON: Forum of Non-Governmental Organizations in Nigeria
notes: FONGON protest at the National Assembly, accusing judges of corruption. At the same time, legislative aides protested at the National Assembly over unpaid allowances.

actor1: MASSOB: Movement for the Actualization of a Sovereign State of Biafra
notes: A group suspected to be members of the Movement for the Actualization of Sovereign State of Biafra, MASSOB, invaded Onitsha main market, beating up traders who were protesting against a market levy.
Unknown gunmen on the night of 04/04 reportedly assassinated a prominent chief in Egbada in Ogba Egbema Ndoni local government area of Rivers State.
Supporters of the Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, demonstrate in Abia to protest an alleged intimidation and molestation from the Nigerian soldiers.

Unidentified gunmen attacked a Police Station in Soro town of Bauchi state, injuring a policeman and destroying the station. Three arrests in connection the attack were made shortly after. The motive of the attack is not known.
Following the killing of a young girl by suspected pirates, residents gather in protest of insecurity of the area.
Militias from Wanikade town and their Wanhihem neighbours clash over the use of farmland between 28/06 and 06/07. 100 + believed dead, property destroyed and 14,000 displaced.
A member of a local group accosts a Hause scrap dealer on 10/01. The attack lead to broader clashes later in the week.
Members of NDA destroy an oil pipeline in Nembe.

Fulani gunmen ambush a group of soldiers on a patrol between Fadan Karshi (Fadan Kaibi) to Karshi Daji. One soldier killed, four injured. The gunmen split into three groups, one continuing into Fadan Kaibi, where they killed 12 villiagers, burnt down 20 houses and injured scores. Another group (or the same, later) went to Karshi Daji, killed 20 people and burnt down several houses. The third group attacked Unguwan Ganye, though casualties are not known.

APC members protest in Mushin Local Government and Odi Olowo Local Council Development Area (LCDA) demanding the expulsion of their party's National Legal Adviser over allegations of embezzlement of campaign funds. The protest took place in Alausa.
Pensioners protest for a second day. No reported violence.
Youths protest the non-availability of election materials or results in Oko Ita.

Suspected Fulani herdsmen stormed Gbemacha council ward (The Guardian claims Mbahimin community, where a recent clash took place) in Gwer East Local Government Area of Benue state, killing an elderly man and three others in a midnight raid on the community.

No fewer than 20 persons were seriously injured and 13 houses torched when a rival youth group attacked another one in Obosi in Idemili North Local Government Area of Anambra State. It was gathered that members of Obosi Youths Movement, OYM, were allegedly protesting the introduction of another youth movement named Obiano Youth Vanguard, with OYM members saying they did not want another youth association in the area.
Two groups of youths violently protest for and against the postponement of an upcoming election. The unrest lasted two days. Several buildings destroyed. One death reported on the first day.
Unidentified gunmen, on 18/05, invaded Rumukwachi community in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State and abducted two residents.
Hundreds of young Nigerians marched on the country's parliament on 25/07, calling for lawmakers to remove age barriers on political posts, including the presidency.
Unidentified attackers laid siege on Tangaran village in Anka local government area of the state on the night of 01/12, killing four.
Doctors stage a demonstration in protest of the abduction and killing of their colleague who had recently been abducted by ransom seeking kidnappers.

After a civilian is decapitated by Fulani attackers in Abraka, locals hold a protest over insecurity by taking the deceased remains to the palace of the Ovie of Oruarivie-Abraka and destroying property. Date of the attack and subsequent protest are not known - source dated 26/04.
Unknown gunmen abducted a Bauchi-based APC politician at his residence in Dario Local Government Area.
A group of Igbo youths protest the outcome of the 28/03 election in Awka, Onitsha, Ekwolobia, Agulu and Nnewi. The protesters blamed the PDP for vote-rigging.

Two soldiers were killed in an explosion that rocked the private residence of Gombe State Governor, Alhaji Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo at Government Reservation Area (GRA), in Gombe metropolis. Attackers are not known.
A coalition of civil society groups from the state gathered the National Assembly to protest a spate of recent killings by Fulanis in Agatu Local Government in Benue State.
Fulanis attack Abi community on 11/02, killing two and causing 19 to go missing.

Clashes between Fulanis and farmers throughout Benue State, namely Agatu, Buruku, Tarka, Kwande, Logo, Makurdi and Guma LGAs, cause mass dislocation of the population. Date within the month and exact locations within the LGAs were not reported.
Special Task Force officers attack a rally organized by the Wase Women Development Association, leaving six injured. The reason for the attack is not known.
Anti-Buhari protesters gather at Unity Fountain for a fourth day. Pro-Buhari counter protesters were also present. No reported violence.
Unidentified gunmen abduct traditional ruler in Isoko South Local Government Area.

Gunmen kill APC deputy ward chairman in Odi in an apparent kidnap attempt, The killing caused tension between the PDP and APC in the area, though it is not clear if any member of the PDP is responsible for the crime.
A group of Igbo youths protest the outcome of the 28/03 election in Awka, Onitsha, Ekwolobia, Agulu and Nnewi. The protesters blamed the PDP for vote-rigging.
A vigilante mob beats a robbery suspect to death in Ihiagwa.
One person has been confirmed dead in Umuobasiukwu in Ozuitem, Bende Local Government Area of Abia State during a clash between Fulanis and unidentified farmers on 12/03.

Victims of the Zaki Biam attacks on 20/03 and 21/03 attack those they believe responsible in nearby Tse-Chia village, near Kasar in Zaki Biam. Three were reportedly burnt alive and several houses were destroyed.
Two suspected robbers are attacked and set alight by a vigilante militia in Nkpor on 22/06.
Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill the head driver of the state governor at Tudun Adabu village in Obi LGA.

Workers at several oil flow stations in Delta State (Olomoro Flow Station, Olomoro Compressor Station, 1 and 2, Oweh Flow Station, Oroni Flow Station, Uzere Flow Station, Uzere Compressor Station, Afiesere Flow Station, Afiesere Compressor Station, Kokori Flow Station, Evwreni Flow Station and Ughelli Pumping Station) walk off the job and protest of unpaid salaries.
A civilian is attacked and killed by suspected Fulani herdsmen as he walked along a road at the riverside town of Torfani in Sagbama local government area. The motive for the attack is not known.

One person was feared dead while two were abducted in a clash between Ijaw community of Ezebiri and their Urhobo counterpart at Furukama in Bomadi and Ughelli South Local Government Areas of Delta State.

One person was shot and wounded in a gun battle on the evening of 14/01 between Ogbe-Ijoh and Aladja communities in Warri South-West and Udu Local Government Areas, Delta State. Reports from the area said the clash took place between 7.48 pm- 7.55 pm at the boundary between the two warring communities.
Suspected Fulanis attack several unnamed villages in Gwer West, killing 35 and over two days. The exact dates are not clear.
Seven vehicles have been burnt by youths from Ohaji/Egbema LGA following the alleged killing of a man by the Imo State Security Network the previous day.
Electrical workers protest over alleged anti-labour practices.
Customs agents protest an increased duty on certain imports.
Gunmen on the evening of 06/06 killed the youth leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC) on 06/06 at the Ikpoba-hill area of Benin City, circumstances not known.
Two labour unions protest at the acting president's office over the increased cost of living.

Residents and traditional rulers of Ozalla community in Nkanu West Local Government Area of Enugu State gathered at Ozalla police station in protest, seeking security agents' protection of the community from alleged impending invasion of the community by herdsmen.

Parents of secondary students enrolled in a public school in Osogbo protest at the office of the headmaster for improved boarding facilities. The group gave a five-day ultimatum before embarking on a mass protest.

Unidentified gunmen, numbering 40, attacked the Maru area of Faru town, Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara, killing two children and injuring their mother. The reason for the attack is not known.

Fulani gunmen ambush a group of soldiers on a patrol between Fadan Karshi (Fadan Kaibi) to Karshi Daji. One soldier killed, four injured. The gunmen split into three groups, one continuing into Fadan Kaibi, where they killed 12 villiagers, burnt down 20 houses and injured scores. Another group (or the same, later) went to Karshi Daji, killed 20 people and burnt down several houses. The third group attacked Unguwan Ganye, though casualties are not known.
One killed, several wounded in a Edo communal clash between those of Uneme and Okpella villages. The clash may have been related to access to a logging area.
Ipetumodu and Asipa communities clash in Ife North LGA. Ten injuries reported.
200 workers of a detergent firm protest their termination. The protest lasted three consecutive days.

Property destruction: Suspected arsonists in the early hours of razed down the office of the Independent National Electoral commission, INEC, in Bori, headquarters of Khana local government area. This development is ahead of the July 30 rescheduled rerun elections in eight local government areas in the state.
Following a murder, a vigilante mob attacks and kills a suspect in Ogboko, Ideato South LGA.
Staff of Imo Broadcasting Corporation protest over pay at the government house on Owerri.
Delta State University, Oleh Campus is closed when students protest the death of three of their colleagues at the hands of a thief.

The people of Ndiabor Umunze in the Orumba South local Government Area of Anambra State, have protest alleged moves to sell their ancestral land at Ohiagu forest in the community. The villagers who demonstrated on the land under the aegis of Ndiabor Progressive Union, NPU, alleged that some politicians are planning to sell the land valued at N200 million to some Abuja-based investors.
Three are killed by unknown gunmen in Makurdi on the evening of 08/08.
Auto parts traders protest in Nkpor over management issues.
Two are killed when a group of 20 unidentified gunmen attacked Eku village, Ethiope East. Additionally, a unnumbered group of NYSC were abducted by the gunmen. Perpetrators not known.

notes: Hundreds of youths from the eight local government areas that make up Rivers West senatorial district protested at the PDP headquarters in Port Harcourt in what they described as the sham primary election of the party for the senatorial district. The group, under the aegis of MOSOP, threatened to boycott an upcoming election. MOSOP held a similar protest in Port Harcourt earlier in the week.
A vigilante mob set a suspected robber alight in the Ogbor Hill area of Aba.
A day following a protest by traders and other residents of Sango decrying the planned demolition of their structures by the state government, a second group gathers and stages a counter-protest.

notes: Indigenes of Edo State under an umbrella group called Concerned Citizens of Edo State protest at the National Assembly Complex against the Edo State Commissioner of Police, alleging 'incompetence.'
Cattle breeders protest a state open grazing prohibition in Jalingo.

assoc_actor_1: NURTW: National Union of Road Transport Workers
assoc_actor_2: RTEAN: Road Transport Employers Association of Nigeria
notes: Members of RTEAN and NURTW clash in Enugu over a court ruling of a motor park.
Lawyers march to the Federal High Court in Port Harcourt denouncing the delay in the appointment of Chief Judge for the state judiciary.

Workers at several oil flow stations in Delta State (Olomoro Flow Station, Olomoro Compressor Station, 1 and 2, Oweh Flow Station, Oroni Flow Station, Uzere Flow Station, Uzere Compressor Station, Afiesere Flow Station, Afiesere Compressor Station, Kokori Flow Station, Evwreni Flow Station and Ughelli Pumping Station) walk off the job and protest of unpaid salaries.
A prominent politician and businessman is shot and killed by unknown assailants.
NUT protesters march to the government house to protest for the release of the Chibok girls.
Hundreds of doctors took to major streets in Lagos, Ibadan, Akure in Ondo State, to protest against the purported sacking of 16,000 resident doctors.
Fulanis kill a farmer in Amagunze over a land dispute on 15/01.

Fourteen, including a teenage girl were reportedly killed in a communal clash between the Jukuns and Hausas in Jalingo of Ibi Local Government Area of Taraba State. Also, no fewer than 40 houses, vehicles and other properties worth millions of naira were destroyed in the bloody clash which erupted at about 4.30a.m. but was later brought under control by a combined team of soldiers and police that were drafted to the area to maintain peace. The clash may have stemmed from a robbery that had been seen a ethnically based earlier in the week.
Igbo youths protest in Enugu to demand police apologise for raiding the Abuja home of the former first lady several months ago.
The women's wing of All Progressives Congress protest the non-release of the Chibok girls by Boko Haram,
Unidentified persons attack a local pastoralist, shooting cows and leaving the victim injured. The attack was believed to have been motivated over the control of farmland.

About 2000 placards carrying youths protest in Port Harcourt the alleged plan by [the current governor] to dissolve the elected council executive in 22 local government areas. The group was sworn in by the former governor.

assoc_actor_1: NANS: National Association of Nigerian Students
notes: Students led by National Association of Nigeria Students, NANS, shut Lokoja, Kogi State capital, protesting the industrial action by lecturers of the State University since May. The protesters blocked vehicular traffic. The protest began the previous day.

A range of forty to sixty reported dead in a clash between Fulani/Alagoa (Fulani mercenaries) and Eggon militias in Tudun-Ababu, Wamba, Akwanga, Nasarawa Eggon - the source records the deaths exclusively at Tudun-Ababu. It was also gathered that all the inhabitants of Assakio, Tudun Adabu and Dedere have deserted their homes as a result of the crisis in the areas. Victims of the troubled areas were seen moving their children and property to Lafia town. Clashes in the area between the two groups has been occurring since 23/08.
Police arrest eight following a clash and destruction of property among residents of Mushin. The reason for the clash is not known.
Striking workers protest non-payment of salaries in Oshogbo.
Residents of Umuode community, Osisoma Ngwa council area, Abia State protest the poor electricity supply and high bills being issued to them by the Enugu Electricity Distribution Company.

A group of armed youths allegedly attacked the Returning Officer for Sadauna Local Government area of Taraba and the Electoral Officer of the area, on their way from Gyembu the headquarters of the local government area to Jalingo the Taraba state capital to submit the local government results. The E O and the Returning Officer were reported to have been abducted by the youths on their way to Jalingo.

Workers at several oil flow stations in Delta State (Olomoro Flow Station, Olomoro Compressor Station, 1 and 2, Oweh Flow Station, Oroni Flow Station, Uzere Flow Station, Uzere Compressor Station, Afiesere Flow Station, Afiesere Compressor Station, Kokori Flow Station, Evwreni Flow Station and Ughelli Pumping Station) walk off the job and protest of unpaid salaries.

Unnamed gunmen attack Ogbele community on 27/02, killing five and kidnapping the chairman of the Community Development Committee. Residents of neighbouring communities fled in fear of mass arrests from descending security forces to the area.

At least 11 persons have been feared killed at Zamadede of Pil-Gani district of Langtang North Local Government Area of Plateau State after unidentified gunmen, suspected to be Fulani, attacked the village during the early morning hours.
Pensioners protest non-payment of salaries.
Hundreds of Echara community indigenes in Nsukka Local Government Area of Enugu State, protested at Enugu Government House a planned creation of a new autonomous community in the area.

Boko Haram (actor not confirmed) attacks a prison in Koton Karifi, overpowers security forces and frees 145 inmates. Two deaths reported, both security forces. Several fugitives were recovered by police in the following days.
Unidentified men murder a Osun Chief on Oshogbo on 25/04. The reason for the killing is not known.

Commercial tricycle operators in Bayelsa State, popularly known as Keke Napep, protested against the alleged excessive use of force and extortion by policemen. The protest comes after police are believed to have mishandled a pregnant woman.
A middle aged woman has been set ablaze for allegedly attempting to kidnap a seven-year-old primary school pupil in Ondo town.

Workers at several oil flow stations in Delta State (Olomoro Flow Station, Olomoro Compressor Station, 1 and 2, Oweh Flow Station, Oroni Flow Station, Uzere Flow Station, Uzere Compressor Station, Afiesere Flow Station, Afiesere Compressor Station, Kokori Flow Station, Evwreni Flow Station and Ughelli Pumping Station) walk off the job and protest of unpaid salaries.
Following an attack on Golgolfa, Fulanis attack several other villages in the LGA. Several houses were destroyed.
10 April. Fulani militia attacked Gbeji Village in Ukum Local Government Area. Seven deaths reported.
An armed gang thought to have come from Chad, attacked the town of Gubio, killing 25 people.
Rioters took to the streets destroying property over the news of the death in jail of political dissident Moshood Abiola. 20 were killed
Ijaw women staged a peaceful march to Government House, Port Harcourt protest the killings in Kaiama; the military occupation and shooting in Yenagoa

Teachers at the Federal Government Girls College, Calabar, on staged a peaceful protest to the Cross River House of Assembly over alleged assault by officers of Department of State Service (DSS).

notes: Health workers under the aegis of the Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals, NUAHP staged a rally in Lagos to protest what they described as 'endemic corruption' in the health sector.
Six students were hurt while protesting a raise in university fees when police sprayed teargas into the crowd.
A student is beheaded on Osogbo, reasons not known. Three suspects were later arrested.

notes: NMA medical doctors working with Osun Government staged protest over the non-payment of salary arrears and poor condition of hospitals.

Hospital patients protest insecurity following a recent robbery in the building.
University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital marched round the hospital lamenting the decay in the facility.
Protest in Kaduna following the termination of a number of state employed teachers.

notes: 3,000 National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members deployed to public secondary schools in Nasarawa state on Monday in Lafia protested over alleged non payment of their state allowances.
Three children were killed and a teacher injured when a man armed with a machete stormed a primary school. Perpetrators not known, though the source references Boko Haram activity in the area.
A college campus gang kills 5 students at Ambrose Alli University.
Lecturers at the Federal University Lokoja hold a strike and protest over non-promotion of staff, among other grievances.

Property destruction: Fulanis attack Ketu area (Imeko-Afon LGA) 'three days after a stakeholders' meeting was held with the state [two weeks ago]' (source dated 5 Feb). The attack destroyed 30 schools.

notes: Members of IBOP disrupt an ECA meeting in Enugu. The members stoned cars, chased journalists, and blocked roads.

Rioters took to the streets destroying property over the news of the death in jail of political dissident Moshood Abiola. University students set 58 prisoners free after storming a prison

Kidnappers abducted a leader of a University, The Attah of Ayede Ekiti Adeleye Orisagbemi.
University students protest the states Agency for Youth and Women Rehabilitation Development (BAYWARD) over payment of N10,000 of monthly allowances.

Students of the American University of Nigeria protest a tuition hike.

University students protest the killing of a student at the hand of a trigger-happy security guard
A lecturer at Tai Solarin University was attacked and killed by suspected cultists.
Unknown gunmen shot and killed an American doctor living in Benin following a church service.
Unknown gunmen break into the home of a journalist, killing him.
Gunmen shoot and kill yet another journalists, despite protests.
A television cameraman operating out of Cross River State is murdered by a group of unknown individuals.
An unknown person pours acid on a university student.
An unidentified gunmen, suspected to be a member of a cult attacked students and teachers at Enugu State University.

For several hours the combined team of security operatives prevented the students of the University of Ado Ekiti, UNAD, from disrupting a public lecture organised by the university, as the students trooped out in large numbers protesting what they described as astronomical hike in school fees.
Gunman have hijacked a school bus in Nigerias Abia state, on the fringes of the oil-producing Niger Delta, and kidnapped 15 children, demanding ransom for their release.

Two Police officers and two journalists with Vanguard newspapers narrowly escaped death, during the evening hours at Shabu village, Nasarawa State when a group of youths, protesting against the death of their colleagues, held them hostage for hours. The demonstration began against speed-breakers along a nearby highway - the protesters barricaded the road with objects and lit fires.

In Lagos, thousands of residents comprising human rights advocates, civil society groups, student union activists and community leaders, among others, stormed the state office of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the state secretariat, protesting voter registration irregularities.
Nigerian police fired shots and used teargas to break up a protest against the military government by several dozen students. 30 were arrested by police.
The body of a radio reporter is found under a bridge. Nothing of value was taken from him, leaving authorities to believe this was a targeted assassination due to his political views.
Three police guards assault an executive of a newspaper and his driver for unknown reasons.
Soldiers seized the cameras of two journalists covering a controversial story.
Gunmen kidnap a journalist in the Delta region.
A Spanish national is kidnapped by unknown gunmen. He is a medical doctor.
Students protest over the suspension of four courses in a popular department. Police shut down the university indefinitely and order the premises vacated to restore order.
Journalists in a restive state in central Nigeria said Monday they would halt coverage of government activities in protest at the failure of the authorities to stop years of deadly violence.

Pupils of Ifelodun Grammar School, Kiloru, were rusticated for carrying out a protest against the trial of an Osun State monarch, Oba Adebukola Alli, Alowa of Ilowa. Oba Adebukola Alli, has been standing trial for allegedly raping a female National Youth Service Corps member, sometime last year.

Nigerian police fired tear gas on Friday in a bid to disperse student protesters demonstrating over a name change at their university, authorities and witnesses said. Students respond by throwing stones at police and physically engaging them. On Wednesday students protesting the name change blocked a bridge elsewhere in the city.
A prominent doctor is kidnapped by unknown men, later released.

Two improvised explosive devices planted under a mango tree behind C block, Naraguta male hostel of the University of Jos, went off on Sunday night while a third explosive connected to the other two was successfully detonated by members of the police anti bomb squad. No report of injury.
Unidentified kidnappers abduct a journalist near his home.
Medical students of Igbinedion University are reportedly abducted.
Unknown men assaulted a journalist in the presence of police, who did nothing to help.
Six students are killed over the weekend by suspected cultists. No name or group given.
rioting students of both LACOPED and LASU destroyed commercial buses and beat up their drivers protesting increased fares and, allegedly, the action of some drivers

Employment of a university protest the non-payment of allowances.
A group of 2,000 university students gathered to protest reported sexual harassment of female students by some staff of the school.
Three protesting Lagos State University students are injured when police break up their demonstration against a delay in university payment.
One is killed when two armed men entered Lagos State University and opened fire on students. Two others injured.
A teachers union protested the cancellation of World Teachers Day by gathering the singing anti-government songs.
Students block the entrance to state offices, preventing the governor and his deputy from entering. The group was protesting an alleged non-payment of their bursary allowances.
Students gather to protest a rate and fee hike of the university. Police react to the demonstration with an increased presence, but to not engage the students.
Classmates of a murdered student protest against the violence, throw stones at police when they attempt to disperse the crowd.
Students at the Osun State College of Education riot in protest of two colleagues killed in a car accident. Fifteen injured, vehicles vandalized.
Students of University of Abuja on Monday protested the failure of the university management to meet up with the six months period given it to accredit some of its courses.

Unidentified gunmen abducted the former Vice Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Prof. Ilochi Okafor. The kidnapping may be political, as Prof. Okafor is a possible gubernatorial candidate in the next election cycle.
Government House security attack a journalist outside the Akwa Ibom State House.
Assassins shoot and kill the Editor of a newspaper, Anambra News, Mr. IK Udendu for unknown reasons.

Students of the Ekiti State University, Ado Ekiti, studying at the satellite location of Kwara State College of Education, Ilorin Outreach Centre protested, claiming they had not received their results to enable them to participate in the forthcoming National Youth Service Corps programme. The group was 500 in number. Traffic was heavily disrupted.
A group of students protest the death of several fellow pupils, victims of a bus crash. The students believed the accident would have been avoided if the road was better maintained.
Ebonyi State University students protest a tuition hike. Police close the university.
A group of secondary school teachers protest the detention of 11 fellow teachers for leading a labour strike. The group also carried place cards demanding greater compensation.
The students of Jigawa College of Education, Gumel, went on rampage and vandalised the institution's vehicles and property during a protest over lack of water supply in the campus.

Police forces attack a group of protesting TASCE students, causing five deaths. However, the police deny this. The provost of TASCE reports one student death. The students embarked on the protest because of the school authority's refusal to allow over 50 per cent of the 200 level students to write examination over the non-payment of tuition fees.

Students of Ekiti State University Ado Ekiti protested against the new policy of no-fee-no-lecture introduced by the university's management. A road leading to the university was blocked by a short time.

A group of aggrieved policemen who were assigned to convey the corpses of their colleagues killed by suspected militants in Bama Local Government Area of Borno State shot a medical doctor in the leg and fired several gunshots to scare medical staff, when they realised that the mortuary was filled to capacity and there was nowhere to deposit the remains of their colleagues.
Students of Olabisi Onabanjo University, Ago-Iwoye, took to the streets to protest the decision of the institution not to allow non-registered students to participate in school activities.

Students of Kwara State Polytechnic protest following the dead of a fellow student at the hands of the police. It is not clear the circumstances of the killing. The protest took place in from of police stations in the Taiwo and Unity areas of the city.
Medical students at the University of Abuja protest a policy that keeps them from graduation. The group demanded N10 million in compensation.

Students of the Anambra State University Igbariam campus protest the killing of a fellow student of armed thieves. The Governor of Amambra State ordered the closure of the school after the students blocked the Igbariam - Awkuzu road and the Enugu-Onitsha expressway. The group accused the school of not providing adequate security for the students.

Unidentified gunmen attack the villages of Goron Dutse, Gwaska and Unguwar Nabango of Birnin Gwari in the early hours of the morning, killing three (some sources claim five deaths) and displacing as many as 3,000. Following the attack the gunmen holed themselves up in a primary school.

Four students of Michael Otedola College of Primary Education were reportedly shot as police tried to disperse protesting students. The students had gathered to protest high student fees. Unconfirmed reports of one student death.

Students of Federal Polytechnic School, Ilaro, Ogun State gather on the Ikorodu expressway in Lagos to protest a long strike caused by disagreement between the Federal Government and academic staff of their school. The students choose protesting on Ikorodu expressway because it is federally managed.
Polytechnic students gather to protest to end an ongoing academic strike along Ikorodu Road in Lagos.
Unidentified gunmen abduct a school teacher. The motovation for the kidnapping remains unknown - there are not call for a ransom payment.

Members of Nigerian Union of Teachers, Ovia North East Local Government Area branch marched through some major streets in Benin, demanding the release of three female teachers who were abducted by unknown gunmen from Orhogbua Primary School, Ekekhuan.
Students block traffic along the Asaba-Benin highway in protest of a ongoing staff-government labour dispute.
Interns at Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, Idi-Araba, Lagos protested non-payment of seven months salaries, disrupting healthcare services.

Around 100 armed youths suspected to belong to a radical OPC faction killed one man when they attacked the Best Hope hospital run by medical doctor Frederick Fasheun, leader of the more moderate faction of the Yoruba nationalist group the Oodua Peoples Congress (OPC)

Students of the University of Nigeria protested against the suspension of the university's Chairman and Pro-Chancellor, Dr. Emeka Enejere, by the Federal Government. The UNN students divided themselves into 11 groups and marched through the major streets of the Enugu metropolis, displaying various placards. It is not clear why Enejere was dismissed.

notes: Activities at both the Nsukka and Enugu campuses of the University of Nigeria, UNN, were paralysed as over 1000 members of the university community abandoned their offices and converged on Nsukka campus to protest the suspension of the institutions Pro-Chancellor, Dr. Emeka Enejere by the Federal Government. It is believed the Chancellor prevented some fraudulent activities by the present administration on campus, as was targeted as a political threat to the bureaucracy. The ASUU had a primary role in leading the protest.

Members of the Nigerian Union of Teachers (NUT) in Kebbi State protested against transfer of primary school teachers salary to Local Government authorities. The protesters took their grievances to the state's House of Assembly demanding a rejection of the Bill sent to the state from the National Assembly.
Unknown assailants kill a farmer in Akure North LGA. Motive of the attack not known; investigators discovered nothing stolen from the victim.
Private schools owners in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State protested the closure of their schools by suspected agents of the state government. The protesters numbered 60.
Protest against a decision to move a local market. The protest continued into the next day.

Ten are dead following a clash between Fulani and Tiv in three villages in Guma LGA, including Tse Uosu, Gbudu and Branch Umenger. The tension began following a robbery incident involving the two groups several days prior.

Governor Ayodele Fayose supporters block streets in protest of against the freezing of his accounts with Zenith Bank by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission. The rally was apparently in reaction to the All Progressives Congress (APC) led anti-Fayose protest held on Thursday.
A group numbering 1000 gather to protest recent Fulani attacks in the area.

Osi and Etan militias clash over two days over 'a long-held dispute.' Two dead, four injured.

Protests against an area ruler in Ikere and Ado-Ekiti.
Protests against an area ruler in Ikere and Ado-Ekiti. The protest in Ikere was a response to a pro-ruler protest the previous day.

Four people are killed at Kamale village in Michika Local Government Area of the state. The MP representing Michika/Madagali Federal Constituency, Adamu Kamale, narrowly escaped the attack. Residents of Gbaji-Seme protest prolonged power outages. Date of the protest not known, source dates 19/11.

Niger Delta youths from the Ijaw ethnic nationality protest over policy at the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission.

Protests in Umuahia and Aba over an election ruling.
Residents of the Okota area protest poor infrastructure.
A pregnant woman is attacked and killed by an armed group described only as militants. Four others injured.

Police disperse a group of violent protesters before they are able to destroy a hotel. The group was protesting the establishments management polices after one of their acquaintances had recently died while swimming at the hotels pool.
