assoc_actor_1: PASAN: Parliamentary Staff Association of Nigeria
notes: Parliamentary Staff Association of Nigeria (PASAN) locked out members of the state House of Assembly in protest over unfulfilled demands bothering on staff welfare.
After a police officer and a meat seller are shot during an argument, a group gathers to protest the violence.

Hundreds of protesters stormed the national headquarters of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and demanded for the immediate resignation of the chairman of the commission after he allegedly refused to investigate a claim of voter fraud.
17 May. Fulanis attack Logo LGA, kill three.
Protest in Ogbunike over excess to public hygienic facilities.
Fulanis attack Mbavuur council ward of Logo Local Government Area, killing six.
Members of a Biafran separatist movement storm a radio station to declare their independence on air, but are pushed back by police forces. Two police deaths resulted from the clash. 13 BZM arrests .
Violent protest in Igando area of Lagos State after a Hausa man allegedly killed (likely in accident) by a commercial bus driver.

12 May. Fulanis clash with an unidentified militia group after it was suspected they were to attack the Agu-Awka area of the city. Causalities not known. The following day, a group of Hausa farmers protested, calling for retaliation against the Fulanis.

17 April: Fulani pastoralist militia killed 15 and left 3 wounded in late night attack on Adamawa communities in Bolki, Bolon, Bujum and Numan towns. They also burned down several houses. Fatalities distributed over 4 locations.
18 May. Protests in Onitsha over a postponed election.
Aladja militia shoots, then abducts a indigene of Egbema/Arogbo community, possibly mistaking the victim for a indigene of Ogbe-Ijoh. The status of the victim is not known.
The village head of Ungwan Muazu in Zazzau Emirate Council is killed by unknown men in Nariya, Kabala West area of Kaduna.
Midwives protest in Asokoro, Abuja over non-payment of allowances.

Youths of Owutu Edda community in Afikpo South Local Government Area of Ebonyi State riot over the shooting of a soldier in the community by policemen (in likely personal dispute). In the melee, property owned by police worth millions of naira was destroyed.

11 March. Communal violence between Okwabang and Beebo communities in Boki East of Cross River State occurs over several days; 11 dead total. The clashes were motivated by land control. The first clash on 08 March caused one death. The following day Beebo militias attacked Okwabang locations killing one. On 11 March Okwabang militias mobilized and attacks Beebo locations killing nine.
Fulanis again attack several communities in Song LGA (the first attack being on 01/02), killing five civilians. Local militia in Simba responded, killing four Fulani.

Arriving on speedboats, militia from Ikot Offiong attacked neighbouring Oku Iboku, Itu Local Government Area; about 20 people killed. Police forces in the area retaliated and pushed the attackers back, killing eight. Despite witness testimony, police leadership denied any Ikot Offiong fatalities.
08 March. Shiites protest for the release of their detained leader at the National Assembly and Unity Fountain.
A gateman attached to a politician (party affiliation not known) in Sime and his kin were killed by unknown gunmen.

Residents of Dan Hono II popular known as Millennium City, Chikun LGA turned out in their numbers to protest what they called forceful taking over of their land by Governor Nasir el-Rufai. The protesters barricaded a road.
Telecommunication subscribers protest in several locations in Abuja over persistent loss of service.

Three persons have been beheaded in the hostility between people of Azuofia Edda Community in Abakaliki Local Government Area of Ebonyi State and Osopong Community of Obubora Local Government, Cross River State. Tensions began after a Obubura resident came to Azuofia and was killed in suspected gang activity.

Armed Fulani men attacked Karmen community in Ibi Local Government Area of Taraba State. In the attack a local traditional ruler was reportedly killed. There is some dispute to the date; either 15/01, 16/01, 17/01.
12 January. Suspected Fulanis attacked Dangaji and Ungwan Gajere villages of Birnin-Gwari LGA over two days, leaving 10 dead. All coordinates approx.
A farmer in Maizaga attacks and kills a Fulani cattle rearer.
Supporters of IPOB protest in Asaba, calling for the release of a jailed leader, Nnamdi Kanu.
Plain cloths militiamen suspected to backed by the government, attacked a group protesting against the ceding of land to Fulani herdsmen for cattle grazing. Extent of injuries not known.
Residents of Akunnu protest after it was alleged a number of Fulanis (not known if militia or civilian) had entered the town.
No fewer than 14 persons are killed and six kidnapped in Sime community in Tai Local Government Area of Rivers State, when gunmen invaded the area on the night of 01/06.
19 May, on or about. A bomb blast of unknown origin detonates in Aba, injuring traders. The event occurred 'at the weekend.'

assoc_actor_1: PENGASSAN: Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria
notes: PENGASSAN oil workers protested at the offices of General Electric (GE) in Lagos and Port Harcourt over the inability of the management to honour collective agreement signed with the organised labour and the Federal Government last year. The protesters reportedly blocked the entrance to each building.
Teachers boycott and protest a government mandated competency exam.
01 September. 4 people, including the APC chairman of Akoko-Edo are abducted by an unidentified armed group in Aiyetoro of Akoko-Edo LGA.

assoc_actor_1: NURTW: National Union of Road Transport Workers
notes: NURTW commercial drivers protest over what they described as 'unhealthy' extortion and harassment of their members by men of Kaduna State Transport and Environmental Agency (KASTELEA).
03 June. Fulanis attack the Tiv community of Dinya (aka Gampu). Local militia however organized and repelled the attack. No reported causalities.
A chieftain of All Progressives Congress (APC) in Akoko- Edo Local Government Area, Edo State is shot and killed by unidentified gunmen along the Igarra-Okpe road on 27/08.
Unidentified gunmen kill 13 at Kyado market in Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.
Four are dead after unidentified assailants entered Ogwashi-Uku and set four residents alight with petrol.

actor1: MEND: Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta
notes: MEND attacks another armed group (likely former members of the sect who in the past had taken part in a government amnesty deal), killing eight. Until recent weeks MEND has been relatively inactive since 2009.

20 March. Employees of local government councils in Benue State, whose names were recently removed from the local government pay vouchers, have staged a peaceful protest to the state's House of Assembly to demand a correction.
Fulani gunmen attack Jootar over four days (07/03 - 10/03), causing five deaths and displacement of several persons.
Library workers protest to demand action to enable the completion of its head office. On the same day, the 'Charly Boy' group protest in Abuja against alleged government graft.
Constituents of Borno South Senatorial District, protested at the National Assembly and blocked roads after their representative was suspended over accusations of fraud.

100 workers of Omala Local Government Area of Kogi State protested over unpaid salaries. According to an eyewitness, the workers stormed the council headquarters in Abejukolo at about 8. 00am, singing war songs and demanding the removal of a local council chairman.
28 September. Women and young people protest in Jos of Plateau State against recent killings and insecurity.
11 May. Youths protest a Senate probe and vote of no confidence passed on Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ibrahim Idris over his failure to appear before the body.

There is tension at Iyana-Iba, around the main gate to the Lagos State University, as hundreds of commercial motorcycle riders have barricaded the entire road leading from Lagos to Badagry area of the state. The motorcycle riders were protesting the seizure of the motorcycles by the state task force.
13 January. Suspected Fulanis attacked Dangaji and Ungwan Gajere villages of Birnin-Gwari LGA over two days, leaving 10 dead. All coordinates approx.

Monarch of Oluasiri community, Ibedaowei of Oluasiri clan in Nembe Local Government area of Bayelsa State, was attacked by five armed men armed with machetes. The monarch was left to die but recovered in hospital.
Supporters of NLC protest in an effort to raise the minimum wage for teachers. Police intervene, fire tear gas.

Members of the Ondo State Council of Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) protested over the pension reforms of the state government. The pensioners barricaded major roads for several hours, before hey converged at the state Accountant Generals office in Alagbaka in Akure.They complained that the pension reforms were causing delays in the payment of their pensions.

After a Ichen man was reportedly killed by unknown persons in his Megoge, Bagi LGA house, the victim's kinsmen blame Tiv, which led to a larger clash between the two groups. Several nearby villages were effected by the unrest, including Gazabu (Bunga), Kungana, Tukun Ruwa, Utsua Daa and Kpenkpen villages, among others. At least 8 reported dead. Other reported dead in the following days.
Pro, anti-SARS protests occurs in Calabar.
Militias from Ugbo and Ugbonla clash in Ugbonla clash for a second day. Injuries reported.
Week of 18 March. Vigilantes attack and kills two suspected criminals in Adani, Enugu.
Youth suspected to support different local factions withi the APC clash in Ilaro at a political rally. One death reported.
Air travellers protest when their fight is delayed.

assoc_actor_1: NULGE: Nigerian Union of Local Government Employees
notes: NULGE members protest unpaid salaries.
Property destruction: 04 June. During the morning hours Fulani and Hausa groups entered Dan Anicha and broke windows of Igbo owned shops.
A protest in support of Olukere of Ikere, a local ruler, occurred in Ikere on 03/01.

Fulani herdsmen attack several Logo villages (Iorzaa, Ukura, Gusa, Per and Gafa) on 25/05 or 24/05 (sources conflict on dates) killing between 50 and 100. The attackers also burned homes and farmlands.
A vigilante mob attacks a suspected ritual killer at a bus stop before being rescued by police.
Nkpor market traders protest higher tax rates at the government secretariat in Ogidi.

Residents in Benin City protest the Chibok abduction. Various groups involved including Widows Association, Brave Heart Initiative, Conference of Non Governmental Organisation (CONGOS) and several others marched round the streets near the capital building.
Indigenes and residents of Umunneochi LGA protest over a petition written by a member of the community against a company located in the area.

Thousands of women of the All Progressives Congress (APC) gathered to protest for the release of the Chibok girls on its one month anniversary. The protesters took off from George Street by 9.30a.m. and walked through the Lagos Island streets to touch base at the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) liaison office at Onikan.

02 June. Fulani militia attacks Kura Falls community in Gashish District of Barkin-Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State on 02/06. The attack was a continuation of an attack in the area the previous day. Three fatalities reported.

actor1: MASSOB: Movement for the Actualization of a Sovereign State of Biafra
notes: Members of MASSOB abduct a Catholic priest in Onitsha, force him to conduct a mass. Police later arrested some of the perpetrators. Date of event vague: at least on or before 14/09.
13 May. A group of Hausa farmers protest a Fulani attack the day before, calling for retaliation against the Fulanis.

Drivers block a highway in protest of area crime.

A vigilante group lynches three suspected kidnappers.

Lecturers at Moshood Abiola Polytechnic, (MAPOLY) Abeokuta, shut the entrance gate of the institution to protest a staffing issue.
12 March. A number of Ado Ekiti students disassociate themselves with a planned anti-government protest, instead holding a counter pro-Fayose protest in Ado Ekiti.

Hundreds of women staged a protest in solidarity with Senator Dino Melaye after an alleged assassination attempt on his life on 15/04. The protesters, who came from the seven local government areas in Kogi West Senatorial District, converged at the Aiyetoro Gbedde residence of Melaye and chanted anti-government songs.
Fulani herdsmen attacked and killed two civilians in Afam-Uku.
Non-academic staff at Lagos State Polytechnic protest after the rector tried to break a labour strike.
Pensioners protest over unpaid arrears.
US citizen and security chief of a Shell station was shot dead at his home in Lagos.
Three gunmen suspected to be assassins have killed the Chief Imam of Egbeta Mosque, in Ovia North East Local Government Area of Edo State on 04/03.
Two persons were confirmed dead when hoodlums suspected to be militants attacked Naval officers at an outpost located at the outskirt of the city of Onitsha.
Members of a Fulani militia reportedly attack and kill a suspected cattle thief in Ikare-Akoko.

Pensioners protest in Owerri over non-payment of arrears.
Okada' riders protest over alleged police harassment in Onitsha.
Factions of two rival political parties (affiliations unknown) clash over the closure of a market. By the time police restored order, eight people were seriously injured.
Over 500 separatists who took part in the declaration of the Republic of Biafra on Monday have been arrested by the police. It is unclear if violence occurred between the actors.
Youths protesting the detention of a group of suspected thieves attempt to burn a police station before they are arrested themselves. Date not clear: source dated 13/08.
05 May. Some members of Ohanaeze Ndigbo, and Igbo cultural group, protest inter-organizational elections in Enugu.

Okada Riders attack a police station, torching five vehicles and seven motorcycles. It is not clear if the police responded.

Some Ozubulu youths under the auspices of Ozubulu Youths Association protested the re-opening of St. Philips Catholic Church, Amakwa Ozubulu, Anambra State. President of the association said it was worrisome that the church would be re-opened for service when investigations into the matter had not been concluded or even the victims buried.
Residents under the aegis IPC protest disillusionment toward their traditional ruler, who they accuse of complicity in murder, arson.
Several groups supportive of President Muhammadu Buhari and Governor Rochas Okorocha march through Owerri. The gathering was in reaction to a planned anti-government protest that never materialized.
26 June. An Igbo group protests for the release of Senator Enyinnaya Abaribe, who was recently arrested for voicing support of IPOB.

A two day clash between farmers and Fulani herders at Akpagodogbo, Otukpa Local Government Area of Benue State causes three deaths. Sources from the area disclosed that trouble started when some cattle belonging to Fulani herders invaded some farms and ate up all the crops in the farms.
09 May. Ezza militia and militia from Abakpa Nike clash in Abakpa Nike and Mbulu-Owo. The violence began after Ezza militia attempted to forcefully take over the areas. Two dead.

Residents of Ngozika Housing Estate, Awka in Awka South Local Government area of Anambra State, on 22/01, took to the streets in protest over what they termed 'exploitation and over-billing' by the Enugu Electricity Distribution Company (EEDC).
The ruler of Mgbuolua in Rundele community in Emohua Local Government Area of Rivers State is kidnapped by unidentified gunmen the morning of 26/12.
Youths stormed the National Assembly and demanded that lawmakers reconvene plenary in the next 10 days or face further, possibly violent, demonstrations.
Military forces shoot six, kill two when residents not complying with an environmental order refuse arrest.
Fulanis attack and kill two civilians in Odonto village in Akpa district of Otukpo Local Government on 23/12. Two others were wounded. Causality figures from multiple sources vary.
Several vehicles were set ablaze in Misau, Bauchi State as protests greeted the appointment of the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Alhaji Ahmed Suleiman, as the new Emir of Misau.

Anti-Rivers State Governor Amaechi protesters, under the aegis of Concerned Citizens of Wakirike Ijaws in Port Harcourt, barricaded the Azikiwe Road, carrying placards and chanting anti-Amaechi songs in reaction to a move by the state government to institute a public holiday to avoid a court indictment that would negatively affect his administration.

notes: IPOB protest in Aba over the detention of a like minded radio personality.
A renews Tiv-Fulani clash claims seven lives.

Tension heightened in Nembe, as aggrieved youths and women forcibly shut down two flow stations belonging to the Shell Petroleum. The group was protesting an unfulfilled promise that electricity and other amenities would be provided to their community.

06 June. Fulanis attack Tse Shan in Saghev, Guma LGA killing eight civilians. The attack was coordinated with a second attack in Logo. A second report from the same source claims 13 dead between the two areas.
Market traders block Uselu/Ugbowo section of the Benin-Lagos highway in protest of a forced market relocation.
Supporters of Ekiti State governor-elect, Ayo Fayose staged a peaceful protest against a potential court ruling that would potentially truncate his authority as governor.

notes: SSANU protests 'anti-union' activities at the University of Abuja.
Unidentified gunmen on motorbikes shot and killed the former police orderly to the Governor. It is unclear if the killing was related to his former political appointment.

Owerri women trooped out in their hundreds to protest the decision of the state government to relocate the Ekeukwu Owerri Market. Protesters gather at a PDP headquarters in Abuja over a conflict of party leadership. It is not known if the protesters were members of the PDP themselves.
Placard carrying directors and professors from the Nigerian Institute of International Affairs protest on Victoria Island over the organizations leadership.

Following the dismissal of an ill student from an Ife-Ife height school, colleagues storm a radio station in protest, assaulting employees and others. The date of the protest is not clear. Source dated 09/05.
Fulanis kidnap three contractors in Onicha on 05/12, reasons not known.

No fewer than seven persons were feared dead in Akokwa community in Ideato North council of Imo State, following a bloody clash between the Hausa/Fulani community and the indigenes of Akokwa.
Traders protest government threats of relocation.

Following the killing of a suspected street gang members, area youths mobilize and burn the house of the suspected perpetrator's father. No human causality reported.
Students of the Federal University, Otuaka protest eviction by their landlords.

An anti-Buhari protest in Port Harcourt is barricaded by police.

A security official said the attack had the hallmark of the Boko Haram.

Military forces engage in a gun battle in Dunamari (Duwabafi) with Boko Haram, four Boko Haram dead.

Suspected Boko Haram members on 20/11 night launched an attack on Kwanti village in Fika local government area of Yobe State, in which 7 persons were killed.
